lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: In Luke 2:11, the angel announces that the Savior was born in the city of David.
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: The angel links the birth to the city of David and to the name Savior.

feedbackWrong.false: See the end of Luke 2:9, when the shepherds were filled with great fear.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.hint: Look at who was born and where, according to the angel.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.question: In Luke 2:10, tap what the angel brings to the shepherds.
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.feedbackCorrect: The angel brings no threat, but good news of great joy.

feedbackWrong.a: That describes the size of the joy, not what he brings.
feedbackWrong.b: That says who the news is for, not what he brings.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.hint: See what the angel says he brings.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.question: According to Luke 2:7, where was the child laid after birth?
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.feedbackCorrect: With no room at the inn, the child is laid in a manger.

feedbackWrong.b: The shepherds were in the fields, but the child was not taken there.
feedbackWrong.c: There was no room for them at the inn.
feedbackWrong.d: The text speaks of the manger, not of a house.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.hint: Read the reason given at the end of the verse.

options.a: In a manger
options.b: In the fields with the shepherds
options.c: In a crib at the inn
options.d: In a house in the city of David

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.question: Put Luke 2:9 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.feedbackCorrect: First the angel comes, then the light surrounds them and fear appears.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who came down to the shepherds.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.hint: Start with who came down to the shepherds.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.question: In Luke 2:8, who was in the fields watching over the flocks?
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.feedbackCorrect: They were field workers, keeping watch during the night.

feedbackWrong.b: The text names who watched over the flocks in that region.
feedbackWrong.c: They are not guards, but those who watched over the flocks.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.hint: Who worked at night in that region?

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.question: What does Luke 2:11 convey that connects to this context?
lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.feedbackCorrect: The joy announced is not for a few, but for all the people.

feedbackWrong.a: The shepherds hear it openly and the sign is given to them.
feedbackWrong.c: The angel speaks of joy for all the people.

lucas-sem-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.hint: See who the angel says the joy will be for.

options.a: News kept in secret
options.b: Good news for all people

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: In Luke 2:8-9, the shepherds receive the angel without fear because they expected the news.
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: On seeing the angel and the glory, they are filled with great fear.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread their reaction in Luke 2:9, before the light and the angel.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.hint: See the shepherds' reaction to the appearance.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.question: In Luke 2:7, tap the word that explains why the child stayed in the manger.
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.feedbackCorrect: This word opens the reason there was no room at the inn.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the place where he was laid, not the reason.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the place with no room, not the word of the reason.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.hint: Look for the word that gives the reason at the end.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.question: How does Luke 2:10 relate to the fear in Luke 2:9?
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.feedbackCorrect: The angel answers the fear with a call not to fear and with joy.

feedbackWrong.a: The news is for all the people, not only for them.
feedbackWrong.b: The shepherds stay and hear the announcement to the end.
feedbackWrong.c: The glory remains and leads to the praise of heaven.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.hint: Compare the feeling in 2:9 with the first words of 2:10.

options.a: The fear proves the news was only for them
options.b: The light drives the shepherds away before the message
options.c: The joy erases the glory they saw
options.d: To great fear, the angel answers with joy

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.question: How does the announcement unfold in Luke 2:10-11?
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.feedbackCorrect: First the fear is addressed, then the news and the birth are announced.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the angel's first words.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.hint: Start with the angel's first words.

options.a: The angel tells them not to be afraid
options.b: He announces good news of joy
options.c: The Savior was born in the city of David

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.question: In Luke 2:13, what did the multitude of the heavenly host do with the angel?
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.feedbackCorrect: Suddenly, a multitude appears with the angel praising God.

feedbackWrong.a: That introduces the words of praise, not its arrival.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes what the multitude does after appearing.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.hint: See the verb that opens the scene of praise.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.question: What links Luke 2:11 to Matthew 1:21?
lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, the child who is born comes to save the people.

feedbackWrong.b: Matthew gives the name Jesus the meaning of saving from sins.
feedbackWrong.c: The sign to the shepherds confirms, but the bridge is salvation.

lucas-cam-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.hint: See the meaning of the name given in Matthew.

options.a: Jesus comes to save
options.b: An ordinary boy in Bethlehem

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.question: Luke 2:10 presents salvation as joy for all the people.
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.feedbackCorrect: The angel says the good news will be for all the people.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread who the good news of great joy will be for.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-01.hint: See the reach of the good news in the verse.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.question: In Luke 2:14, tap what the praise gives to God in the highest.
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.feedbackCorrect: The praise begins by giving glory to God in the highest.

feedbackWrong.b: Peace is announced for the earth, not given in the highest.
feedbackWrong.c: The earth receives peace; it is not what is given to God.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-02.hint: See the first word of the praise.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.question: What reading does Luke 2:10-11 support about the Savior's coming?
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.feedbackCorrect: Announced to shepherds and for all the people, the Savior reaches simple folk.

feedbackWrong.b: The text gives purpose to the announcement and the sign to the shepherds.
feedbackWrong.c: Heaven praises at this birth, a sign of God's presence.
feedbackWrong.d: The announcement to shepherds shows the opposite of prestige as a door.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-03.hint: Compare who hears with the reach the angel states.

options.a: God brings salvation reaching simple people
options.b: The announcement to shepherds was mere chance
options.d: Salvation is only for the prestigious

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of the announcement in Luke 2?
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.feedbackCorrect: News to the simple reveals the Savior and ends in praise and peace.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who receives the news in the field.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-04.hint: Start with who receives the news in the field.

options.a: God announces good news to the humble
options.b: The Savior is born for all the people
options.c: Heaven praises and speaks of peace

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.question: In Luke 2:11, which name shows what the child came to do for the people?
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.feedbackCorrect: The name Savior sums up the mission of the child who was born.

feedbackWrong.a: Christ is the title of the sent one, but saving is in the other name.
feedbackWrong.b: Lord shows authority, but the name of the mission comes first.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-05.hint: It is the name tied to what he came to do for the people.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.question: What links Luke 2:14 to Isaiah 9:6?
lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah announces a ruling child, and Luke speaks of peace on earth.

feedbackWrong.a: Isaiah links peace to the rule of the child who is born.
feedbackWrong.c: The praise is to God, and peace comes to earth through the child.

lucas-pro-lc-01-salvador-humilde-06.hint: See who Isaiah says is born and rules.

options.a: Peace without a ruler
options.b: Peace brought by the child

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: In Luke 15:4, the man who loses a sheep waits at home until it comes back on its own.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: He leaves the ninety-nine and goes after the one that was lost.

feedbackWrong.true: He stays home waiting for the sheep to come back by itself.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-01.hint: See what he does after losing a sheep.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-02.question: In Luke 15:5, tap where the man puts the sheep when he finds it.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-02.feedbackCorrect: Once found, the sheep is carried on his shoulders with joy.

feedbackWrong.b: That marks the moment of finding, not where it is placed.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes his joy, not the sheep's place.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-02.hint: See what he does as soon as he finds it.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.question: According to Luke 15:8, what does the woman do when she loses a drachma?
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.feedbackCorrect: She lights up, sweeps and searches carefully until she finds it.

feedbackWrong.b: The neighbors are called only later, to celebrate.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of buying, but of searching at home.
feedbackWrong.d: She searches herself until she finds it, without waiting for it back.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-03.hint: Read her three actions in the verse.

options.a: Lights the lamp and searches carefully
options.b: Asks the neighbors to sweep the house
options.c: Buys another drachma at the market
options.d: Waits for someone to return the coin

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-04.question: Put Luke 15:4 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-04.feedbackCorrect: He has a hundred, loses one, leaves the others and searches until he finds it.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the owner of the hundred sheep.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-04.hint: Start with the owner of the hundred sheep.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-05.question: In Luke 15:9, what does the woman say she has found?
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-05.feedbackCorrect: It was one of her ten drachmas, sought throughout the house.

feedbackWrong.a: She did not lose a key, but part of what she had saved.
feedbackWrong.c: The name Jesus uses in the story is another, more specific one.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-05.hint: Think of the second story in the scene.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-06.question: What does Luke 15:6 convey that connects to this context?
lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-06.feedbackCorrect: The finding becomes a party shared with friends and neighbors.

feedbackWrong.a: He gathers friends and neighbors to tell of the finding.
feedbackWrong.b: He searches precisely because the sheep has worth to him.

lucas-sem-lc-02-misericordia-06.hint: See who he gathers when he gets home.

options.a: A search done in secret
options.b: A loss of no value at all

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: In Luke 15:6-7, the joy of the one who finds the sheep points to joy in heaven over a sinner who repents.
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus links the party at home to joy in heaven over the repentant.

feedbackWrong.false: The party ends at home, with no echo at all in heaven.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-01.hint: See the application Jesus makes in the next verse.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-02.question: In Luke 15:8, tap the word that shows how hard the woman searches.
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-02.feedbackCorrect: She searches diligently, not giving up until she finds it.

feedbackWrong.a: That says how much she had, not how she searches.
feedbackWrong.c: The lamp is the tool of the search, not the way of searching.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-02.hint: Look for the adverb that describes how she searches.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-03.question: How does Luke 15:5 relate to Luke 15:4?
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-03.feedbackCorrect: The search in 15:4 ends in finding and care in 15:5.

feedbackWrong.a: He is the one who goes to seek and carry; she does not return alone.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says he finds it and puts it on his shoulders.
feedbackWrong.c: He searches until he finds it, without giving up.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-03.hint: See the outcome of the search begun in the previous verse.

options.a: The sheep returns to the flock alone
options.b: The search ends without finding the sheep
options.c: The owner gives up at nightfall in the field
options.d: The one who searched joyfully carries what he found

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-04.question: How does the story unfold in Luke 15:8-9?
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-04.feedbackCorrect: The loss leads to an earnest search, and the finding becomes a celebration.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what is lost inside the house.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-04.hint: Start with what is lost inside the house.

options.a: One drachma out of ten is lost
options.b: The woman searches the whole house

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-05.question: In Luke 15:7, over whom is there more joy in heaven when they change course?
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-05.feedbackCorrect: Heaven rejoices over one sinner who repents.

feedbackWrong.a: The one who wanders off is the lost before the finding, not the reason for the party.
feedbackWrong.c: The finding is celebrated openly, not hidden.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-05.hint: See the condition tied to joy in heaven.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-06.question: What links Luke 15:4 to Ezekiel 34:11?
lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-06.feedbackCorrect: In Ezekiel, the Lord himself says he will search for his sheep.

feedbackWrong.b: The earnest search shows the worth of the one who was lost.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts, the sheep need to be sought.

lucas-cam-lc-02-misericordia-06.hint: See who sets out to search in both texts.

options.a: God himself seeks the lost
options.b: Being lost does not matter

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.question: Luke 15:7 teaches that God rejoices more over those who never err than over the repentant sinner.
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.feedbackCorrect: The text states the opposite, with joy over the repentant.

feedbackWrong.true: True, since the righteous are always the main reason for the party.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-01.hint: Compare who causes more joy in heaven.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-02.question: In Luke 15:10, tap where there is joy over a sinner who repents.
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus places the joy before the angels of God.

feedbackWrong.a: That is who repents, not the place of the joy.
feedbackWrong.c: That links the stories; it does not say where there is joy.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-02.hint: Look for the place of this joy at the end of the scene.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-03.question: What reading does Luke 15:7 support about God before the repentant sinner?
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-03.feedbackCorrect: God's joy answers the sinner who repents and comes back.

feedbackWrong.a: The text celebrates one without despising the rest of the flock.
feedbackWrong.b: The joy is precisely over a sinner who repents.
feedbackWrong.d: The stories show God seeking, not just waiting.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-03.hint: See the reason for joy that Jesus states.

options.a: God despises the ninety-nine righteous
options.b: God rejoices without calling to repentance
options.c: God celebrates the return of the lost
options.d: God waits for the lost to come back alone

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of the searches in Luke 15?
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-04.feedbackCorrect: From the search on earth to joy in heaven, Christ came to save sinners.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the search Jesus tells about.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-04.hint: Start with the search Jesus tells about.

options.a: The sheep is sought until it is found
options.b: There is joy in heaven over the repentant
options.c: Christ came into the world to save sinners

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-05.question: In Luke 15:10, what is there before the angels of God over a repentant sinner?
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-05.feedbackCorrect: Before the angels of God there is joy over the repentant.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of a party in heaven, not of silence.
feedbackWrong.c: Fear is not the reaction described for this moment.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-05.hint: See heaven's reaction in both stories.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-06.question: What links Luke 15:10 to 1 Timothy 1:15?
lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul sums up the mission: Christ came into the world to save sinners.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, sinners are the aim of salvation.
feedbackWrong.c: The joy is over sinners who repent and come back.

lucas-pro-lc-02-misericordia-06.hint: See who Paul says Christ came to save.

options.a: Joy with no repentance at all
options.b: Christ came to save sinners

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: In Luke 9:51, Jesus firmly resolved to go to Jerusalem as the time of his ascension drew near.
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: The decision is firm and shows on Jesus' face.

feedbackWrong.false: He hesitated and left the destination for the disciples to choose.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.hint: See the decision made in the verse.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.question: In Luke 9:48, tap who Jesus says is truly great.
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus reverses the measure: the least is the one who is truly great.

feedbackWrong.a: That says in whose name to receive, not who is great.
feedbackWrong.c: The child is the example welcomed, not the answer about greatness.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.hint: Look for the contrast at the end of the verse.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.question: According to Luke 9:49, why does John say they forbade a certain man to cast out demons?
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.feedbackCorrect: The reason John gives is that the man did not follow with them.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus corrects the ban in the next verse.
feedbackWrong.b: The text mentions no charging of money in this scene.
feedbackWrong.d: He acted in Jesus' name, according to John's account.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.hint: Read the reason John himself gives.

options.a: Because Jesus had told them to forbid it
options.b: Because he asked the people for money
options.c: Because he did not go with the group

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.question: Put Luke 9:52-53 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.feedbackCorrect: Messengers prepare lodging, but the village does not receive Jesus.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with who Jesus sent ahead.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.hint: Start with who Jesus sent ahead.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.question: In Luke 9:50, what does Jesus tell them not to do to the man casting out demons?
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus says not to forbid whoever is not against them.

feedbackWrong.a: Receiving appears in the teaching about the child, not in this command.
feedbackWrong.b: Following the group was the disciples' demand, not the final word.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.hint: See the first word of Jesus' answer.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.question: What does Luke 9:48 convey that connects to this context?
lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus values the least and the child received in his name.

feedbackWrong.a: Receiving the child in his name is receiving Jesus himself.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus places greatness in the least, not in being served.

lucas-sem-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.hint: See who Jesus calls great at the end.

options.a: A child has no worth
options.b: Greatness seeks to be served

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: In Luke 9:48, Jesus teaches that greatness among the disciples is measured by being the best known in the group.
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus measures greatness by the least, not by standing out in the group.

feedbackWrong.true: True, since he points to the best known as great.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.hint: Compare the group's measure with Jesus' final word.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.question: In Luke 9:53, tap the word that opens the contrast with preparing lodging.
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.feedbackCorrect: The small opening word turns the scene toward rejection.

feedbackWrong.b: That explains the reason; it does not open the contrast.
feedbackWrong.c: That says whose appearance it was, not the contrast.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.question: How does Jesus respond in Luke 9:50 to the attempt to forbid one who did not go with the group?
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus widens their view and tells them not to forbid him.

feedbackWrong.a: The man already acted in Jesus' name, with no change requested.
feedbackWrong.b: He does not drive the man away, but corrects the disciples.
feedbackWrong.d: His words go against keeping the work only within the group.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.hint: Read Jesus' short answer to John.

options.a: He changes the name the man used
options.b: He orders the man out of the village
options.c: He does not accept the group's ban
options.d: He says only the group may act

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.question: How does the scene unfold in Luke 9:51-52?
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.feedbackCorrect: The firm decision becomes a journey, with messengers ahead.

feedbackWrong.default: The Samaritan rejection closes this movement.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.hint: The Samaritan rejection closes this movement.

options.a: Jesus firmly resolves to go to Jerusalem
options.b: Messengers go to prepare lodging

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.question: In Luke 9:53, what did the Samaritans not do with Jesus?
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.feedbackCorrect: They did not receive him, seeing he was going to Jerusalem.

feedbackWrong.a: The problem is not hearing, but welcoming him for lodging.
feedbackWrong.c: Follow is not the verb used for the refused lodging.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.hint: See the verb that is negated right at the start.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.question: What links Luke 9:48 to Mark 10:45?
lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.feedbackCorrect: The Son of Man came to serve, and the least is the great one.

feedbackWrong.a: Mark shows the Son of Man serving, not ruling.
feedbackWrong.b: Jesus' service reaches everyone, not only leaders.

lucas-cam-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came to do in Mark.

options.a: Greatness by bossing others
options.b: Service only for leaders

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.question: Luke 9:51 shows Jesus heading to Jerusalem with firm resolve even in the face of rejection on the way.
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.feedbackCorrect: The decision is firm even before the village refuses lodging.

feedbackWrong.false: The decision vanishes at the first refusal.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-01.hint: See the strength of the decision before the messengers are sent.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.question: In Luke 9:51, tap the phrase that shows Jesus' decision about Jerusalem.
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.feedbackCorrect: The decision is firm and visible on Jesus' face.

feedbackWrong.b: That names the destination, not the act of firmly deciding.
feedbackWrong.c: That speaks of the time drawing near, not of the decision.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-02.hint: Look for the verb of decision in the middle of the verse.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.question: What reading does Luke 9:54 support about James and John's reaction?
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.feedbackCorrect: Faced with refusal, they propose fire against the Samaritans.

feedbackWrong.a: The question comes from the disciples, not from an order by Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: The fire proposal goes against the spirit of the earlier teaching.
feedbackWrong.d: Those who suggest fire are James and John, not the Samaritans.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-03.hint: See who speaks and what they propose in the verse.

options.a: Jesus asked them to call down fire
options.b: Rejection stirred in them a desire for revenge
options.c: They understood the teaching about the least
options.d: Samaritans asked for fire against Jesus

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.question: Which sequence reveals the meaning of the journey in Luke 9?
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.feedbackCorrect: From the least being valued to the firm path, Jesus serves by giving his life.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the teaching on greatness.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-04.hint: Start with the teaching on greatness.

options.a: Jesus values the least of all
options.b: He firmly resolves to go to Jerusalem
options.c: The Son of Man gives his life

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.question: In Luke 9:48, what does Jesus call the one who is least of all?
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus calls the least great, against the grain of the group.

feedbackWrong.a: Least describes the condition, not Jesus' final verdict.
feedbackWrong.c: First suggests a fight for position, absent from the final sentence.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-05.hint: Contrast it with the word least in the same sentence.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.question: What links Luke 9:51 to Isaiah 50:7?
lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah speaks of a face set like flint, and Luke shows Jesus resolved on the way.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus decides to go; he does not flee his destiny in Jerusalem.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus' firmness does not turn into revenge on villages.

lucas-pro-lc-03-caminho-jerusalem-06.hint: See the image of the set face in both texts.

options.a: Fleeing from rejection
options.b: A face set in obedience

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: In Luke 24:46, Jesus states that the Christ had to suffer and rise on the third day.
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Suffering and resurrection on the third day were written.

feedbackWrong.false: The resurrection was only to happen much later.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.question: In Luke 24:45, tap what Jesus opened in the disciples so they could understand the Scriptures.
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus opens their understanding so they grasp the Scriptures.

feedbackWrong.b: That marks the step in the scene, not what Jesus opens in them.
feedbackWrong.c: The Scriptures are what they come to understand, not what is opened in them.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.hint: Look for what changes inside the disciples.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.question: According to Luke 24:44, where was written what had to be fulfilled about Jesus?
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus gathers the Law of Moses, the Prophets and the Psalms about himself.

feedbackWrong.a: The Psalms are only one of the three parts Jesus names.
feedbackWrong.c: Bethany appears at the departure, not as a source of the writing.
feedbackWrong.d: The letters did not yet exist in this talk of Jesus.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.hint: Read the three parts named in the verse.

options.a: Only in the Psalms of David
options.b: In the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms
options.c: In a book kept in Bethany

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.question: Put Luke 24:44 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: Jesus recalls his words and points to the Law, Prophets and Psalms.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the reminder of what he had already said.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.hint: Start with the reminder of what he had already said.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.question: In Luke 24:48, what does Jesus call the disciples in view of what they saw?
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: They saw, and now they are witnesses of these things.

feedbackWrong.a: That is their general name, but Jesus uses another word for the mission.
feedbackWrong.c: The text highlights the role of telling what they saw.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.hint: What does he name them for the task ahead?

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.question: What does Luke 24:47 convey that connects to this context?
lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: Beginning at Jerusalem, the proclamation reaches all nations.

feedbackWrong.b: The text ties the proclamation precisely to repentance.
feedbackWrong.c: Jerusalem is the start, not the limit of the proclamation.

lucas-sem-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.hint: See how far the proclamation must reach.

options.a: Repentance for all nations
options.b: Forgiveness with no repentance

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: In Luke 24:47, the proclamation was to stay limited to Jerusalem without reaching other nations.
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Jerusalem is the starting point for all nations.

feedbackWrong.true: True, since beginning at Jerusalem means ending there.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.hint: See whether Jerusalem is a limit or a start in the verse.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.question: In Luke 24:45, tap the word that marks the next step after Jesus speaks.
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: This word opens Jesus' next action with the disciples.

feedbackWrong.a: That is what Jesus opens, not the link to the earlier words.
feedbackWrong.b: That is what they understand, not the step marker.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.hint: It is the first word of the verse.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.question: How does Luke 24:45 relate to Jesus' words in Luke 24:44?
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: After citing what was written, Jesus opens their understanding.

feedbackWrong.a: He returns to the Scriptures and explains them by opening their minds.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says he needed to open their understanding.
feedbackWrong.c: The resurrection confirms his earlier words; it does not cancel them.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.hint: See Jesus' action right after citing what was written.

options.a: Jesus sets the Scriptures aside
options.b: The disciples already understood everything alone
options.c: The earlier words are canceled by the resurrection
options.d: Jesus opens their minds to grasp what was written

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.question: How does the plan unfold in Luke 24:46-47?
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: From what was written about Christ comes the proclamation to all nations.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what was written about the Christ.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.hint: Start with what was written about the Christ.

options.a: The Christ suffers and rises on the third day
options.b: Repentance is proclaimed in his name

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.question: In Luke 24:49, with what would the disciples be clothed from on high?
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: They must wait in Jerusalem until they are clothed with power.

feedbackWrong.b: Signs go with the mission, but the gift named is another.
feedbackWrong.c: The clothing here is not ordinary garments.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.hint: See the gift that comes from on high while they wait.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.question: What links Luke 24:48 to Acts 1:8?
lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: In Acts, the witnesses go from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.

feedbackWrong.b: Luke already calls the disciples witnesses sent to proclaim.
feedbackWrong.c: Acts links witness to the power of the Holy Spirit.

lucas-cam-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.hint: See how far the witnesses go in Acts.

options.a: Witnesses to the ends of the earth
options.b: Witness kept in Jerusalem

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.question: Luke 24:43 shows a merely spiritual Christ who could not eat in front of the disciples.
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.feedbackCorrect: Luke says he took the food and ate in front of them.

feedbackWrong.true: True, since a risen body is never shown eating.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-01.hint: See Jesus' concrete action in the verse.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.question: In Luke 24:46, tap the phrase that shows suffering was part of what was written.
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.feedbackCorrect: Jesus presents suffering and resurrection as necessary in what was written.

feedbackWrong.a: That marks the time of the resurrection, not the necessity of the plan.
feedbackWrong.c: That says from where he rises, not the necessity stated.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-02.hint: Look for the words that speak of necessity in the plan.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.question: What reading does Luke 24:46-47 support about the cross of Christ?
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.feedbackCorrect: It was written that the Christ would suffer and rise.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus links the cross to what was written, not to a detour.
feedbackWrong.c: The proclamation that comes from it is one of repentance.
feedbackWrong.d: It all starts from what is written in the Scriptures.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-03.hint: See what Jesus says was written.

options.a: The cross was a defeat outside the plan
options.b: Suffering was in the announced plan

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.question: Which sequence reveals the plan that runs through the Scriptures?
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.feedbackCorrect: From the suffering servant to the resurrection, the message reaches the nations.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the ancient promise of the servant.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-04.hint: Start with the ancient promise of the servant.

options.a: The servant suffers for sinners
options.b: The Christ rises on the third day

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.question: In Luke 24:47, which word names the forgiveness tied to repentance?
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.feedbackCorrect: Repentance is proclaimed for the remission of sins.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of remembering sins, but of their remission.
feedbackWrong.c: The proclamation announces forgiveness, not a charge for sins.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-05.hint: It is tied to what happens to sins.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.question: What links Luke 24:46 to Isaiah 53:5?
lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah describes the servant wounded for our transgressions.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, the suffering has a purpose for others' sins.
feedbackWrong.b: Luke places the suffering before the glorious resurrection.

lucas-pro-lc-04-vitoria-ressurreicao-06.hint: See for whom the servant suffers in Isaiah.

options.a: Suffering with no purpose at all
options.b: Glory without going through suffering

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Luke 15:5, on finding the lost sheep, the man puts it on his shoulders with joy.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: The finding ends in care and joy, on his shoulders.

feedbackWrong.false: He leaves it in the field because he is tired from searching.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-01.hint: See his gesture on finding the sheep.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Luke 2:11, tap who was born in the city of David.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: The one born is the Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the final title, but the name of the mission comes earlier.
feedbackWrong.b: That says where he was born, not who was born.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-02.hint: See the central name in the angel's announcement.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-03.question: According to Luke 24:48, what does Jesus say the disciples are?
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: Jesus calls them witnesses of what they saw in him.

feedbackWrong.a: Bethany is the place of departure, not the disciples' role.
feedbackWrong.b: The mission is to proclaim, not to judge the nations.
feedbackWrong.c: Jesus opens the Scriptures; they do not own them.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-03.hint: Read Jesus' short sentence to the disciples.

options.a: Guardians of Bethany
options.b: Judges of the nations

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-04.question: Put Luke 2:10 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: The angel calms them, announces joy and opens its reach to all the people.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the angel's first words.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-04.hint: Start with the angel's first words.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Luke 9:48, what does Jesus call the one who is least of all?
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: For Jesus, the least is the one who is truly great.

feedbackWrong.b: Small describes appearance, not Jesus' verdict.
feedbackWrong.c: Last points to the fight over positions that Jesus corrects.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-05.hint: See the verdict at the end of the teaching on the child.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-06.question: What does Luke 15:6 convey that connects to this context?
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: Friends and neighbors are gathered to celebrate the finding.

feedbackWrong.a: The search shows how much the sheep is worth to its owner.
feedbackWrong.b: He calls others to tell them, not hiding his joy.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See who is gathered when he gets home.

options.a: A loss of no value at all
options.b: A search done in secret

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Luke 24:49, tap what the disciples would be clothed with.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: The Father's promise clothes the disciples with power from on high.

feedbackWrong.b: That says who sends the promise, not what clothes them.
feedbackWrong.c: That says where to wait, not what clothes them.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-07.hint: See the gift that comes from on high in the promise.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-08.question: Put Luke 15:8 in the order of the text.
lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: Ten drachmas, one lost, a search of the whole house until it is found.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the total the woman had.

lucas-sem-lc-boss-revisao-08.hint: Start with the total the woman had.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: In Luke 9:50, Jesus orders them to forbid the man casting out demons without going with the disciples.
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus says the opposite, telling them not to forbid him.

feedbackWrong.true: True, since he defends the group's exclusivity.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-01.hint: Read Jesus' short command to John.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Luke 15:7, tap the word that links the sheep story to joy in heaven.
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: This word bridges the story and its application in heaven.

feedbackWrong.b: That is who repents, not the link to the story.
feedbackWrong.c: That describes the joy, not the linking word.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-02.hint: Look for a short word right after Jesus begins.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-03.question: How does the announcement in Luke 2:10 answer what the shepherds felt in Luke 2:9?
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: To their fear, the angel tells them not to be afraid, with joy.

feedbackWrong.a: They hear the whole announcement and receive a sign.
feedbackWrong.c: The joy announced is for all the people, including them.
feedbackWrong.d: The glory remains and the heavenly host appears afterward.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-03.hint: Compare the first feeling with the angel's first words.

options.a: The shepherds are sent away in silence
options.b: Words of joy come to great fear
options.c: The fear proves the news was not for them
options.d: The light vanishes before any word

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-04.question: How does the search unfold in Luke 15:4-5?
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: Loss, earnest search and a caring finding form the arc.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what is lost from the flock.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-04.hint: Start with what is lost from the flock.

options.a: One sheep out of a hundred is lost
options.b: The owner searches until he finds it
options.c: He carries it on his shoulders

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Luke 24:45, what did Jesus open so the disciples could understand the Scriptures?
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: Jesus opens their understanding and they grasp the Scriptures.

feedbackWrong.a: Way describes the journey, not what is opened in them here.
feedbackWrong.c: The word Luke uses names the ability to understand.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-05.hint: See what Jesus opens in them, according to Luke.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-06.question: What links Luke 9:48 to Mark 10:45?
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: The least is great, and the Son of Man came to serve.

feedbackWrong.a: Jesus' service is not limited to those who lead.
feedbackWrong.c: Mark presents Jesus serving and giving his life.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See what the Son of Man came to do in Mark.

options.a: Service only for leaders
options.b: Greatness by serving others

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Luke 2:7, tap the word that explains why the child stayed in the manger.
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: The word opens the reason there was no room at the inn.

feedbackWrong.a: That is the place with no room, not the word of the reason.
feedbackWrong.c: That is where he was laid, not the word of the reason.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-07.hint: Look for the word of the reason at the end of the verse.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-08.question: How does the conversation unfold in Luke 24:44-45?
lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: From recalling what was written, Jesus opens their understanding.

feedbackWrong.default: The understood Scriptures are the point of arrival.

lucas-cam-lc-boss-revisao-08.hint: The understood Scriptures are the point of arrival.

options.a: Jesus recalls what was written
options.b: He opens the disciples' understanding
options.c: They come to understand the Scriptures

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.question: Luke 24:46-47 presents suffering, resurrection and proclamation to the nations as one announced plan.
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.feedbackCorrect: Jesus himself links what was written, the cross, the resurrection and the nations.

feedbackWrong.false: They are loose facts with no link in Jesus' words.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-01.hint: See how Jesus weaves the three points together.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-02.question: In Luke 15:10, tap where there is joy over a sinner who repents.
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-02.feedbackCorrect: The joy happens before the angels of God.

feedbackWrong.a: That links the stories; it does not show the place of joy.
feedbackWrong.b: That is who repents, not the place of the joy.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-02.hint: Look for the place of this joy at the end of Luke 15.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-03.question: What reading does Luke 9:51 support about Jesus on the way to Jerusalem?
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-03.feedbackCorrect: The decision is firm and visible before the Samaritan rejection.

feedbackWrong.a: The text shows a conscious decision, not someone dragged along.
feedbackWrong.b: He sends messengers and keeps the chosen course.
feedbackWrong.c: The rejection comes later, and he had already resolved to go.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-03.hint: See the strength of the decision before the rejection.

options.a: He is led without knowing where he goes
options.b: He gives up the way when refused
options.d: He goes on with firm, obedient resolve

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-04.question: Which sequence reveals Luke's thread from birth to mission?
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-04.feedbackCorrect: From humble birth to seeking and sending, Luke shows the Savior.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the announcement of the birth.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-04.hint: Start with the announcement of the birth.

options.a: The Savior is born in the city of David
options.b: The lost are sought and celebrated

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-05.question: In Luke 15:7, over whom is there joy in heaven when they change course?
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-05.feedbackCorrect: A sinner who repents is the reason for joy in heaven.

feedbackWrong.a: The finding is celebrated with others, not hidden.
feedbackWrong.b: The one who wanders off is lost before the party of finding.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-05.hint: See the condition tied to joy in heaven.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-06.question: What links Luke 24:48 to Acts 1:8?
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-06.feedbackCorrect: Luke's witnesses go to the ends of the earth in Acts.

feedbackWrong.b: Acts joins witness and the power of the Holy Spirit.
feedbackWrong.c: The calling is meant to be proclaimed, not kept.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-06.hint: See how far the witnesses go in Acts.

options.a: Witnesses to the ends of the earth
options.b: Mission without the Spirit

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-07.question: In Luke 24:46, tap the phrase that shows suffering was part of what was written.
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-07.feedbackCorrect: Suffering and rising were necessary in the written plan.

feedbackWrong.b: That marks the time of the resurrection, not the necessity.
feedbackWrong.c: That says from where he rises, not the necessity.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-07.hint: Look for the words of necessity in the written plan.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-08.question: Which sequence reveals God's care running through Luke?
lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-08.feedbackCorrect: From God's search to the sending of witnesses, the lost are reached.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the search credited to the Lord himself.

lucas-pro-lc-boss-revisao-08.hint: Start with the search credited to the Lord himself.

options.a: The Lord seeks the lost sheep
options.b: Jesus celebrates the repentant sinner
options.c: Witnesses take repentance to the nations
